liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugar Magnolia** (3 reviews, 1 other source): Mickey Hart nearly kicked over his drums during the opener's jam; the song was reportedly chosen as Bill's favorite; Opening with it felt right; the crowd cried, and a week later the memorial closed with Sunshine Daydream [6][13][15][22]
- **Mona** (2 reviews, 2 other sources): Santana and Gary Duncan joined the band for Aiko Aiko and Mona; Jerry began singing 'Hey Bo Diddley' before Bobby took over the lyrics; Duncan and Santana played strongly [1][6][12][15]
- **Althea** (3 reviews): The Althea was blistering; Althea is singled out as a standout, with Touch Of Grey, amid very high energy [16][18][22]
- **Touch Of Grey** (1 review): The 'we will survive' line ending the first set was a touching moment [15]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The China Cat into I Know You Rider is masterful [18]
- **Knockin' On Heaven's Door** (1 review): The encore was touching and appropriate, leaving the Coliseum crowd in tears [13]
- **Masterpiece** (1 review): Reviewer considers the Masterpiece alone worth downloading the show [20]

## Setlist highlights

- **David Graham Speech**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [23]
- **Mona**: back after 598 archived shows (2931 days); rare: 3 archived performances [23]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-10-27.137738.sbd.miller.us.dat.flac1648** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 186 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1991-10-27.sbd.gmb.81199.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 178 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [7]
- **gd91-10-27.sbd.martinson.537.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 4.86/5 by 35 [8]
- **gd1991-10-27.139300.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 179 min [2]

## Around the show

- Bill Graham had died a day or so earlier; wreaths decorated the stage and David Graham addressed the crowd after the first set [12]
- Reviewer recalls the helicopter crash and rain surrounding this strange period [14]
- Nobody knew what to expect two days after the shocking news; the show became a celebration of Graham's life [16]
- The second set featured guest jams [16]
- After losing Bill, the band played the show as tribute and celebration of him [20]
- The band seemed stunned yet rose to the occasion, playing each first-set song as a tribute to Bill [22]
- Carlos Santana and Gary Duncan of Quicksilver played guitar on Iko Iko and Mona [1]
- First Dead show after Graham's death in the helicopter crash; the night was very somber [6]
- A week later the band played Sunshine Daydream at Golden Gate Park [12]
- Reviewer ranks it among the best of 1991 [18]
- Unlike other big occasions said to be cursed, this one went well [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-10-27.137738.sbd.miller.us.dat.flac1648**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Dat Master (48k) [1]
- **gd1991-10-27.sbd.gmb.81199.sbeok.flac16**: taped by DAT source provided by B.Koucky (rec'd from B.Fried 1996).; transferred by Transfer, mastering and lossless encoding by C.Ladner.; source: SBD > DAT(48KHz) > DAT playback on Sony PCM-R500 > XLR analog outputs > Mogami Gold cables > Neutrik inputs, Presonus Firebox (pre-amplification and… [7]. Also: The first notes of Sugar Magnolia are clipped, as on another circulating source; The encore audience splice was taken from a previously circulated set [7]
- **gd91-10-27.sbd.martinson.537.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD> DAT> ZA2> Soundforge 4> CD Architect> CDR> EAC> shn [8]
- **gd1991-10-27.139300.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100/Tascam Deck) [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1991-10-27 Grateful Dead Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1991-10-27-grateful-dead-backstage-pass/) [24]
